stage: domain M / domain E interface, step 10 (bridge testing) and step 12 (falsifiers)
topic: Brahui leave-one-out geographic measurement
failed_output: A leave-one-out geographic measurement over attested Dravidian languages was interpreted as showing something about where Dravidian was spoken, and specifically as making Brahui's northwestern position anomalous and in need of a migration explanation. Recorded in full at DMB-001.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure. A delete-one statistic computed over a set with one extreme member measures the influence of that member on the statistic. Reporting the remainder is a sensitivity report about the instrument. Converting it into a claim about a language family's geography is the step-10 bridge failure in its exact form: the link from 'the statistic moves a long way when this element is deleted' to 'this element is anomalous in the history' is a separate claim and was never made, let alone tested.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: It assumes that the set of attested Dravidian languages is a sample of Dravidian geography. It is a sample of survival. The languages attested today are the ones that were not replaced, and the archive that records them is the colonial and post-colonial survey record, which enumerated speech communities it reached and classified. Deleting Brahui does not simulate a Dravidian world without Brahui; it simulates the record we would hold if one more replacement had run to completion. Under the step-6 archive audit that is the whole question, and the statistic assumes it away.
affected_claims: DMB-001 (superseded), DMB-002 (restatement); bears on IH-135 / hypothesis H-01, IH-031, IH-156 / rejected row R-10; and on the reading of DME-022 and DME-023
correction: DMB-001 is SUPERSEDED and retained, not deleted. DMB-002 restates the claim to the two things the statistic can carry: the instrument's exposure to one datapoint, and the size of the gap between Brahui and the next-nearest attested Dravidian language. Unit 2 supplies the arithmetic (DMB-010 to DMB-013) by computing the delete-one influence of all twenty attested varieties, so that Brahui's influence is reported against a distribution rather than on its own.
future_control: No leave-one-out, jackknife or delete-one statistic in this repository is reported without (a) the per-element influence of every element, not only the element of interest, and (b) an explicit statement of the reference point or estimand and of who chose it. A delete-one result reported for one element alone is a sensitivity claim presented as a finding.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: The reading of DME-022 and DME-023 as bearing on donor-language geography. Those rows are corpus-internal and correctly scoped, but DME-023 states a compatibility with 'the greater Indus and north-west' whose own geographic reference point is not stated numerically. Queued as RA-004. Also the inherited rows IH-031, IH-135 and IH-156, which carry the burden-of-proof argument this measurement was being used inside; queued as RA-005.

stage: domain M, step 4 (evidence classes kept separate) and step 10 (bridge testing)
topic: North Dravidian subgrouping and the independence assumption
failed_output: A Euclidean distance from each attested Dravidian language to a northwestern reference point, with the languages treated as independent observations and Brahui read off as an isolated outlier.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure with a bias consequence. A distance-to-reference statistic has no term for shared descent, so it cannot represent a clade. If Brahui, Kurukh and Malto subgroup, their three positions are not three observations; they are one observation of an ancestor's location plus whatever happened afterwards. Treating them as three both inflates the apparent support and makes Brahui look like it stands alone when it may be the northwestern member of a group that also reaches Jharkhand. A second and separate defect: Euclidean distance over a latitude/longitude pair is not a distance on the earth, and its error is a function of latitude, which is exactly the axis the northwest/south contrast runs along.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: The representation is not neutral. Rendering a language family as a scatter of points in a plane is the representation in which 'Brahui stands alone' is true by construction, because the representation has deleted the only structure - descent - that could make it not stand alone. Choosing that representation and then reading a historical verdict out of it is a case of the instrument supplying the conclusion. The pull is bidirectional and must be named as such: an isolated northwestern outlier can be talked up as a relict of an early northwestern distribution, or talked up as a recent arrival. Neither follows from the scatter, and the prestige-bias and preferred-counter-narrative tests both bite here.
affected_claims: DMB-001 (superseded), DMB-005; and every claim that treats Brahui's position as evidence in either direction, including IH-135 / H-01
correction: Unit 2 measures the thing the statistic could not see. Exclusive cognate sharing across Brahui, Kurukh and Malto is computed from a retrieved cognate-coded Dravidian dataset (SRC-049) and reported against every other pair and triple in the same dataset (DMB-017 to DMB-022), so the subgroup is measured rather than assumed. The contested status of the subgroup is recorded separately at DMB-023 to DMB-026 rather than folded into the measurement.
future_control: Any measurement over two or more languages in this repository states, in the claim row itself, whether it assumes the languages are independent observations, and if the languages are claimed to be related it names the tree it assumed or records that it used none. Any planar distance over geographic coordinates reports the great-circle distance alongside it, or is not reported.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: The same reaudit targets as BF-005: RA-004 for DME-023's unstated geographic reference, RA-005 for the inherited Brahui rows. Additionally, no earlier work in this repository has ever used a phylogenetic assumption, so there is no prior tree-based claim to reaudit; that absence is itself why the control above is written as a positive requirement rather than a correction.

stage: Extraction and counting, pur- 4J corpus unit, 2026-09-07
topic: Whether a numeral in a Rigvedic stanza counts the fort word
failed_output: A mechanical numeral-noun agreement test scored on case, gender and number, which returned PARTIAL for navati- 'ninety' and would have excluded five of the six passages stating ninety-nine forts.
bias_or_method_failure: Deference to the reproducible instrument over the reading. The test was scriptable, auditable and wrong: navati- is a feminine SINGULAR collective ('a ninety') governing a plural puraḥ, so it agrees in case and gender and never in number. Following the instrument would have produced a tidy, re-runnable, false result — and one that happened to minimise the ninety-nine, which is also the direction of this project's available soft landing.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: Machine-checkable output carries more institutional prestige here than a philological judgement, because this repository's whole design privileges reproducibility. That is right as a default and wrong in this instance, and the design does not by itself flag the exception.
affected_claims: PUR4J-004; PUR4J-005; PUR4J-I-01; every COUNTS-PUR verdict on a navati- row in 03-REGISTERS/rigveda-pur-counts.csv
correction: The three instruments (agreement, proximity, translation) are carried in their own columns and a separate verdict column records the reading. Six rows carry an instrument_override cell naming which instrument the verdict overrides and why. Nothing was silently corrected.
future_control: Any mechanical agreement test over Vedic morphology must be checked against collective and governing numerals before its output is used. More generally: when an instrument and a reading disagree, the register carries both columns rather than the winner.

stage: Interpretation, pur- 4J corpus unit, 2026-09-07
topic: Whether the Rigvedic fort counts are formulaic
failed_output: PUR4J-007 as first written: 'Sambara's forts are counted at ninety, ninety-nine, one hundred, the hundredth and hundreds across six passages. Every count value the constitution section 4J enumerates attaches to this one opponent.' It was VERIFIED and it was the strongest of the four diagnostics behind PUR4J-I-01.
bias_or_method_failure: PREFERRED-COUNTER-NARRATIVE FAILURE, caught by the independent reviewer and not by this unit's own section 8.2 test. Three of the five values were wrong, and all three errors ran the same way — toward the deflationary conclusion that the counts are formulaic. (1) RV 1.130.7's ninety are broken FOR Puru and Divodasa, datives; Sambara stands in a separate clause with no genitive attaching the forts to him. The row rested on Sambara merely occurring in the stanza — the exact inference PUR4J-006 and the counts register's own note declare invalid, in the same unit. (2) 'The hundredth' had already been withdrawn as a fort count by this branch's own COUNTS-SERIES-COMPLETION fix, which reworded three other claims and missed this one. (3) 'Hundreds' at RV 6.31.4 was a misreading of satani against three unanimous translators and against this register's own treatment of the identical form at RV 1.53.8.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: Not archival. The pull is that instability is the interesting result: a count that varies is evidence for formula, and the unit had already named formulaicity as its available soft landing and built four controls against adopting it. Three of those controls held. The one that failed is the one that interrogated the CONCLUSION rather than re-deriving the EVIDENCE, which is the specific weakness of an adversarial test run by the author.
affected_claims: PUR4J-007 (restated, demoted to PROVISIONAL); PUR4J-002, PUR4J-003 and PUR4J-009 (the 'hundreds' member removed; 100 now stated in 9 passages, not 8); PUR4J-I-01 diagnostic prediction 1 (restated from FAILS to INCONCLUSIVE)
correction: PUR4J-007 now claims only what survives: ninety-nine in three passages and one hundred in two, five passages and two values, and those two values are the pair PUR4J-008 argues are one schema. PUR4J-I-01's prediction 1 is downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE and the interpretation's support is restated as two clear diagnostics of four rather than three.
future_control: An author-run adversarial test must re-derive its own load-bearing evidence from the text, not interrogate the conclusion drawn from it. Concretely: any claim of the form 'value X attaches to entity Y' must cite the syntax that attaches them — a genitive, an agreement, a governing numeral — and never stanza co-occurrence, in a unit that has itself proved co-occurrence invalid.
earlier_work_requiring_reaudit: None outside this unit. Within it, every claim citing PUR4J-007 was traced and restated; PUR4J-I-01 is the only interpretation affected.

stage: 13-PRODUCT-ARCHITECTURE/experience-object-model.md, preferred-counter-narrative challenge re-run at document scope after BF-022 showed the first pass had been run only where review had already pointed
topic: Experience object model — route order in §11.4, and the limit of §13.9's prohibition on inventing voice
failed_output: Two findings. (1) §11.4's rule that a Journey's order can be an assertion was illustrated with one example only — a route running steppe to Punjab to the Ganges — which is the canonical migration account. A rule given one example is read as aimed at that example, and the same rule bites at least as hard on a route running one Indian site to the next in an unbroken sequence, which asserts continuity or autochthony more quietly because a route that never leaves is read as no route at all. (2) §13.9 specified the fabrication failure in full and its converse nowhere: as written it could be read to refuse a living community's own attested account of ancestors the colonial archive did not record, on the ground that the record does not carry them.

Finding 2 is the mirror failure and the more serious: an anti-fabrication rule, which is a good rule, operating as a silencing rule against the one evidence class the archive systematically excluded.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: Finding 2 rests on treating nameability in a written archive as the test of whether a person can be spoken about. That is the archive's own test, and adopting it reproduces the exclusion this document had just finished documenting. The correct test is who is speaking and on what authority: an institution speaking for the unrecorded is fabricating; a community speaking for itself is giving oral-living evidence under framework §2.4 and §11.2.

stage: 13-PRODUCT-ARCHITECTURE/water-living-world.md §9.1a, preferred-counter-narrative challenge, found in adversarial re-review of the first repair pass
topic: Whether a LANGUAGE Living World has an ANCIENT PROBLEM slot and an ECOLOGICAL CHANGE slot
failed_output: §9.1a asserted that "LANGUAGE breaks two slots outright": that a language thread "has no problem being solved" and no environmental change, so slots 1 and 4 are inapplicable rather than unevidenced. On that basis §3.3 gained an inapplicable field, §3.4 invariant 2 was said to be satisfied by it, and WLW-012 cited it as one of five grounds. The claim was asserted from one paragraph of introspection, with no register row and no test.
bias_or_method_failure: Method failure with a counter-narrative edge, and the second consequence is the serious one. (1) Slot 1 is defined as "What did people have to solve, where, and when?" - not "what environmental hardship did they face". Recording speech, administering a multilingual polity, transmitting a liturgy without writing and mutual intelligibility across a trade network are ancient problems with material, epigraphic and textual evidence. (2) Slot 4 is worse: environmental and demographic change is the standard mechanism in language-spread argument, and this repository's own IH-138 ties post-urban settlement movement to a weakening monsoon. Declaring slot 4 inapplicable to a LANGUAGE world would mean such a world never has to place its environmental claim in the slot governed by M-4's date types and museum framework §4.4's bridge rules - removing the one position where the environmental-determinism bridge must be statused, in the document whose §4.4 requirement 3 exists to catch that bridge.
archival_or_institutional_assumption: That the domain tags in §3.2 ("environment + settlement" for slot 1) define what a slot admits. They are this document's own gloss, and §9.1b concedes the tag vocabulary is not even a valid enum - so a design decision was taken on the authority of a column the same document had already found unsound.
affected_claims: WLW-012 (fifth ground, withdrawn); water-living-world.md §3.3 (inapplicable field, withdrawn), §3.4 invariant 2, §9.1a
correction: The inapplicable field is removed from §3.3 and the invariant-2 claim with it. §9.1a is demoted from a finding to a candidate observation, restated as the question a second world would answer, with both counter-readings stated. WLW-012 drops the ground. The field would have been a slot that disappears when empty, which §3.1 of the same document exists to prevent.
future_control: A design field is not added on the strength of a hypothetical instance reasoned through in prose. Where a second world is invoked to justify a change to the pattern, the invocation is written as a candidate observation until a world is actually expressed in the slots and the result recorded. And any proposal that removes a slot from a world is checked against what that slot was policing before it is accepted.
